mgmt_team_view.text: A 20-year Nestle veteran, Navratil took the CEO role in September 2025 after the sacking of Laurent Freixe and set out 16,000 job cuts, lifting annual savings to CHF 1bn by end-2027 within the wider cost programme. First-half 2026 brought organic growth of 3.6% with real internal growth of 1.5%, net profit of CHF 3.5bn and free cash flow of CHF 3.4bn, though net profit fell 31% on a CHF 1.3bn write-down tied to businesses being sold. Capital allocation has centred on pruning: a 50:50 waters joint venture expected to yield about CHF 2.8bn, vitamins and ice cream held for sale, yfood bought out and Blue Bottle divested.

citations.quote: - Guidance for 2026: Organic growth expected in the range of 3% to 4%, with UTOP margin expected to improve versus 2025.

sentences.text: Nestle is concentrating its portfolio on four core businesses, Coffee, Petcare and Nutrition, which together account for about 70% of sales, plus leading regional positions in Food and Snacks.
Coffee is its largest business with leadership in every zone and three billion-dollar brands, Nescafe, Nespresso and Starbucks, in a category expected to grow 3-5% in value between 2025 and 2027.

sentences.text: A RIG-led growth model is gaining traction, with first-half 2026 organic growth of 3.6%, real internal growth of 1.5% and pricing of 2.1%, and full-year guidance of 3-4% organic growth with an improved underlying trading operating profit margin versus 2025.

thesis_pillars.text: A RIG-led growth model is gaining traction, with first-half 2026 organic growth of 3.6%, real internal growth of 1.5% and pricing of 2.1%, and full-year guidance of 3-4% organic growth with an improved underlying trading operating profit margin versus 2025. Emerging markets are the main growth engine, delivering 7.1% organic growth excluding China, while China has stabilized. Cost savings of CHF 600 million in the first half and strong free cash flow with lower net debt support reinvestment.
